catalog.label: Instrument-air low-pressure indication at RHOB receiving header P-R triggered alarm AL-44 and paused work.
catalog.detail: At approximately 10:00 AM on May 20, 2024, the RHOB process area reported loss of instrument-air pressure while a two-person Utilities team was preparing the #1 slab caster (1SC) compressor/dryer system for planned maintenance. The work was paused and the air supply was subsequently restored.

catalog.label: Utilities air gallery distributes instrument air to the RHOB process area. The receiving header H-R at RHOB has a local indication point P-R that typically displays within a normal operating range (above 5.0 bar).
catalog.detail: The Utilities air gallery distributes instrument air to the RHOB process area. The receiving header H-R at RHOB has a local indication point P-R that typically displays within a normal operating range (above 5.0 bar).

catalog.label: Alarm AL-44 activates when P-R pressure drops below 4.5 bar and clears above 5.0 bar.
catalog.detail: The RHOB PLC low-pressure input from point P-R (AL-44) is configured to trigger a 'COMP FAULT' indication if the measured pressure falls below 4.5 bar, and it resets when pressure rises above 5.0 bar.

catalog.label: At 10:00 AM, P-R pressure dropped from ~6.8 bar to below alarm thresholds (<4.5 bar).
catalog.detail: RHOB operations detected an instrument-air low-pressure indication at the receiving header (P-R), dropping from approximately 6.8 bar to a value that triggered the AL-44 alarm.

catalog.label: Work package WO-527-E field execution record was blank at folder issue.
catalog.detail: The work package cover indicates the temporary instruction attachment field and the field execution record (WO-527-E) were both left blank when issued, meaning no specific instructions or updated drawings were attached to guide boundary preparation.

catalog.label: Maintenance acceptance signature was not yet signed at notification time.
catalog.detail: The work package cover explicitly states that the maintenance acceptance signature field had not been filled in when the incident occurred, indicating the boundary preparation phase was incomplete or unverified by receiving operations.

catalog.label: Personnel U-A and U-B held current operating qualifications at shift start.
catalog.detail: Both crew members were listed with 'Current Utilities operating qualification' and energy-control authorization, confirming they met the baseline competency requirements for their assigned tasks.

catalog.label: Utilities acknowledged the alarm at approximately 10:02 AM and paused work.
catalog.detail: Upon receiving notification of the low-pressure indication, Utilities operations formally acknowledged the issue around 10:02 AM and immediately halted all maintenance activities pending further review.

catalog.label: Work was paused and air supply restored by approximately 10:07 AM.
catalog.detail: By about 10:07 AM, the local indication at RHOB returned to normal band levels. The incident description notes that work had been paused earlier but does not specify whether full restoration of service or just a temporary pressure recovery occurred before maintenance was deferred until later (by 10:20).

catalog.label: P-U remained stable at 6.8–6.9 bar while P-R dropped.
catalog.detail: The upstream supply was unaffected by the event that caused pressure loss downstream.

catalog.label: AL-44 activates below 4.5 bar and clears above 5.0 bar.
catalog.detail: The alarm threshold configuration accounts for why AL-44 triggered at ~10:00 when pressure fell to 5.8 bar then dropped further.

catalog.label: Pressure and alarm data are sampled values (~30–40 seconds), not continuous waveforms.
catalog.detail: The discrete sampling means the exact time of pressure drop is inferred from drops between samples (e.g., 6.8→5.8 at 10:00:11).

catalog.label: The area directory does not establish valve positions or pressure availability at any given time.
catalog.detail: This document serves as an administrative index and lacks operational data on physical states like open/closed valves.

catalog.label: Shift log records 'boundary preparation in progress' but does not identify point of interruption or valve states.
catalog.detail: The shift log confirms work was paused at 10:02 due to an air-low indication, yet it lacks details on whether the Utilities crew had isolated a specific line or if RHOB observed a leak before pausing.

catalog.label: No engineering disposition or temporary instruction was attached for changes to instrument-air service affecting RHOB between 2024-03-01 and May 20, 2024.
catalog.detail: Per IA-D03 Section 3.6, an approved change record is required before using a modified arrangement on a maintenance boundary. Absence of such documentation suggests either no change occurred or one was used without formal approval (unknown).

catalog.label: Daily briefing topic line reads '1SC dryer work and RHOB service coordination' but contains no valve-by-valve content.
catalog.detail: The crew may not have received explicit instruction on current valve states or recent routing changes, contributing to uncertainty about the system configuration during boundary preparation.

catalog.label: No evidence of documented confirmation between Utilities and RHOB that the air-low alarm was understood.
catalog.detail: While communication occurred (RHOB requested attendance at 10:02), there is no record confirming whether both parties agreed on the cause or immediate corrective action before pausing work.

catalog.label: Potential unrecorded service-routing change or undocumented valve state created a unique hazard scenario.
catalog.detail: Hypothesis: An unauthorized valve closure upstream of P-R (e.g., M-101/M-102) could have isolated RHOB without updating records. Requires verification against engineering drawings and work orders.

catalog.label: Crew U-A/U-B collected WO-527 work folder and lock equipment at 09:35; boundary preparation in progress by 09:48.
catalog.detail: Standard pre-maintenance steps were followed, but the absence of a verified system configuration check (e.g., valve status confirmation) before starting work may have contributed to vulnerability when pressure dropped.

catalog.label: Maintenance receiver M-A had boundary acceptance pending at shift start.
catalog.detail: Per IA-D02, 'maintenance released' refers to work-boundary acceptance. Pending status implies the Utilities crew retained control until formal release.

catalog.label: Alarm AL-44 display text 'COMP FAULT' retained from earlier template; mapped to receiving-header pressure condition per PR-12.
catalog.detail: The label does not reflect the actual cause (pressure loss vs. compressor fault), potentially delaying troubleshooting if operators assumed a mechanical failure rather than investigating supply-side issues first.

catalog.label: C-11 RUN is a running-status bit; not a local flow proof.
catalog.detail: The 'RUN' indicator remained active despite pressure loss, confirming the compressor motor was energized but unable to maintain header pressure. This rules out immediate mechanical seizure as the primary cause of P-R drop.

catalog.label: Pressure values are bar gauge; point register needed to interpret location and scope.
catalog.detail: P-U (upstream) stability vs. P-R drop confirms the issue was downstream of H-U, likely in the distribution path between North gallery and RHOB receiving header.

catalog.label: Handwritten records are approximate unless stated otherwise.
catalog.detail: Shift log entries like 'About 10:07' lack precise timestamps, introducing uncertainty about exact restoration time and response duration.

catalog.label: RHOB process area receives instrument air from Utilities gallery via receiving header H-R.
catalog.detail: Normal operation involves pressure monitoring at P-R (receiving station) and upstream P-U. Alarm AL-44 monitors low-pressure condition below 4.5 bar.

catalog.label: Pressure extract IA-P01 provides sampled values only (not continuous) and excludes data from all locations or valve states.
catalog.detail: Export covers P-U, P-R, C-11 RUN but lacks full waveform coverage. Cannot confirm simultaneous events at other points like North gallery without additional evidence.

catalog.label: Point register IA-P02 does not establish state of any distribution valve.
catalog.detail: Register maps signals (P-U, P-R, C-11 RUN, AL-44) but explicitly states it cannot prove supply disturbance appearance in sample export or valve positions.
